resolveScreenTheme.about: A screen theme as every client reads it (issue #194, docs/screen-theme-v1.md): what it says over the defaults; a part it can't read falls back to that part's defaults, a field it doesn't know is ignored, and anything that isn't a theme is the default look.

cases.name: a few fields: the rest default
a bad colour: that part's defaults, the rest kept
a field from a later version: ignored
a grid (issue #268): a widget of a kind from a later version, or that can't be read, leaves its cells empty
a grid that can't be read: none, the words fill the screen
layers (issue #280): a base colour, the camera, a widget moved to the overlays, masks - one that can't be read left out

pickDaySet.about: The set a screen following its owner's schedule shows (issue #274): among today's, the one going on (started within 3 hours, the latest), else the next to start, else the latest that started; none today: null.

cases.name: the only one today, before it starts
morning and evening, during the morning one
morning and evening, in the afternoon: the evening one
late at night: the evening one, the latest started
without a time: as if at midnight

orderScreenSets.about: The owner's sets as a screen offers them (issue #274): upcoming by date and time, then undated, then the archive, the latest first.

screenWidgetLayer.about: The layer a widget is on (issue #280): its own, else its kind's - the widgets that show the song are content, the others overlays.

cases.name: the song's details, moved to the overlays

screenBaseColor.about: A theme's base colour (issue #280): its own, else its background's first, as before layers.

placeScreenWidget.about: Where a client draws a widget (issue #268): its cells kept inside the grid, whatever the template says.

cases.name: past the right and bottom edges: cut to fit
starting outside a smaller grid: its last cell

screenQrPayload.about: What a QR code widget encodes (issue #289): an address as it is, an event as an iCalendar VEVENT, a contact as a vCard 3.0, a Wi-Fi network as WIFI:. Null while there's nothing to encode.

screenSlideCount.about: Where the Slide count widget says the screens are (issue #289): the slide shown out of the song's, or out of the whole set's. Null when nothing's shown.

cases.name: the first slide of the set
an item without words, nothing shown
a slide past the song's end: nothing

screenLayoutPresets.about: The ready-made grids a template's layout starts from (issue #268), by id.

readScreenTimer.about: What a countdown or count up widget shows (issue #268): its seconds, past zero or not, near the end or not, running or not - from the operator's timer, a length from when the set item came on, a time of day, or the song on screen. Null when there's nothing to count.

cases.name: the operator's countdown, paused near the end: warned
the operator's countdown, past zero: counting on
no operator timer: nothing to show
a length from when the item came on
a count up since the song came on

timerColors.about: A countdown's or count up's colours by time (issue #272): its break points when it has some, else amber near the end and red past zero; null for its own.

cases.name: no break points, near the end: amber
no break points, past zero: red
break points at 5:00 and 1:00, 400 s left
break points at 5:00 and 1:00, 200 s left
break points at 5:00 and 1:00, 45 s left
break points at 5:00 and 1:00, 0 s left
break points, past zero: the lowest
a count up not there yet

formatTimer.about: Seconds as a timer shows them: m:ss, h:mm:ss past an hour, a + in front past zero.

screenThemeTemplates.about: The built-in themes, by id, in full: a client that offers them shows these.

screenThemeContrast.about: The lowest contrast between a theme's words and what's under them (WCAG 2, 1 to 21); an outline, shadow or glow counts as half again. An editor warns under 4.5.

cases.name: dark grey on black, no effect
a picture: mid-grey under the words unless darkened

sectionEnergy.about: How lively a part is, from its label, for a background that warms up in a chorus: high, mid or low.

normalizeScreenCode.about: A pairing code as typed, as it's kept: upper case, no spaces or dashes; null when it can't be one.

cases.name: typed in lower case with a space
